act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Definitions — small quantity and commercial quantity
section_desc: 'Small quantity' means the quantity specified in column 5 of the table appended to this Act. 'Commercial quantity' means the quantity specified in column 6 of that table. For cannabis: small quantity = 100 grams (charas/resin) or 1 kg (seeds/leaves); commercial quantity = 1 kg (charas) or 20 kg (seeds/leaves). For heroin/morphine: small quantity = 5 grams; commercial quantity = 250 grams. For cocaine: small quantity = 2 grams; commercial quantity = 100 grams. For methamphetamine: small quantity = 2 grams; commercial quantity = 50 grams.

act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Punishment for contravention in relation to manufactured drugs and preparations
section_desc: Whoever, in contravention of any provision of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder, manufactures, possesses, sells, purchases, transports, imports inter-State, exports inter-State or uses any manufactured drug or any preparation containing any manufactured drug shall be punishable: if small quantity — up to 1 year imprisonment or fine up to Rs 10,000 or both; if more than small quantity but less than commercial quantity — up to 10 years and fine up to Rs 1 lakh; if commercial quantity — not less than 10 years, extendable to 20 years plus fine not less than Rs 1 lakh.

act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Punishment for contravention in relation to psychotropic substances
section_desc: Whoever, in contravention of any provision of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder, manufactures, possesses, sells, purchases, transports, imports inter-State, exports inter-State or uses any psychotropic substance shall be punishable: if small quantity — imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs 10,000 or both; if more than small quantity but less than commercial quantity — up to 10 years and fine up to Rs 1 lakh; if commercial quantity — not less than 10 years extendable to 20 years and fine not less than Rs 1 lakh.

act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Punishment for external dealings in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in contravention of section 12
section_desc: Whoever engages in or controls any trade whereby a narcotic drug or psychotropic substance is obtained outside India and supplied to any person outside India shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to twenty years and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to two lakh rupees.

act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Punishment for allowing premises, etc., to be used for commission of an offence
section_desc: Whoever, being the owner or occupier or having the control or use of any house, room, enclosure, space, place, animal or conveyance, knowingly permits it to be used for the commission by any other person of an offence punishable under any provision of this Act, shall be punishable with the rigorous imprisonment and fine provided for that offence.

act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Punishment for consumption of any narcotic drug or psychotropic substance
section_desc: Whoever consumes any narcotic drug or psychotropic substance shall be punishable: if it is cocaine, morphine, diacetylmorphine or any other narcotic drug or any psychotropic substance — with rigorous imprisonment up to one year or fine up to Rs 20,000 or both; if it is cannabis (except ganja) — up to 6 months or fine up to Rs 10,000 or both.

act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Punishment for financing illicit traffic and harbouring offenders
section_desc: Whoever indulges in financing, directly or indirectly, any of the activities specified in sub-section (2) of section 2, or knowingly harbours any person who has committed an offence punishable under this Act, shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to twenty years and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to two lakh rupees.

act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Presumption of culpable mental state
section_desc: In any prosecution for an offence under this Act which requires a culpable mental state of the accused, the Court shall presume the existence of such mental state but it shall be a defence for the accused to prove the fact that he had no such mental state with respect to the act charged as an offence in that prosecution. Reverse burden of proof — accused must prove absence of mens rea.

act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Offences triable by Special Courts
section_desc: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, all offences under this Act which are punishable with imprisonment for a term of three years or more shall be triable only by the Special Court constituted for the area in which the offence has been committed or where there is no Special Court, by the Court of Session.

act: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
section_title: Power of Magistrate to issue warrant for search
section_desc: A Magistrate of the first class or a Magistrate of the second class specially empowered in this behalf by the State Government may, by warrant, authorise any officer of any of the departments mentioned in section 42 to enter and search any building, conveyance or place, to seize any article liable to confiscation under this Act, to detain and search and arrest any person in or about such building, conveyance or place, who is found to be in possession of any narcotic drug or psychotropic substance.

section_title: Definitions
section_desc: In this Act: 'ammunition' means ammunition for any firearm and includes grenades, bombs and other like missiles; 'arms' means articles of any description designed or adapted as weapons for offence or defence and includes firearms; 'firearms' means arms of any description designed or adapted to discharge a projectile by the action of any explosive and includes air guns; 'prohibited arms' means firearms so designed or adapted that they can be fired in a fully automatic mode; 'prohibited ammunition' means ammunition designed or adapted for use with prohibited arms.

section_title: Licence for acquisition and possession of arms
section_desc: No person shall acquire, have in his possession or carry any arms (other than firearms) of a class or description specified in Schedule I to this Act unless he holds in this behalf a licence issued in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Such arms include swords, spears, lances, daggers, bayonets and like weapons. Certain traditional ceremonial weapons of Sikhs are exempt.

section_title: Licence for manufacture, conversion, repair, test or proof of arms or ammunition
section_desc: No person shall manufacture, convert, repair, test or prove any arms or ammunition, or convert any imitation firearm into a firearm, unless he holds in this behalf a licence issued in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.

section_title: Grant of licences
section_desc: The licensing authority shall grant a licence under Chapter II (1) for acquisition, possession and carrying of any firearm or ammunition, if it is satisfied that the person is not prohibited by law from acquiring or possessing arms, is not of unsound mind or convicted of specified offence, and that there is no likelihood of his using the arms or ammunition for any unlawful purpose. The number of firearms any person can hold on a single licence is limited to one (maximum two in exceptional cases).

section_title: Renewal of licences
section_desc: A licence granted under Chapter II shall be renewed at such intervals and in such manner as may be prescribed. A licence holder shall apply for renewal at least two months before the expiry of the licence period. Failure to renew renders possession unlawful. State Governments typically require renewal every three years for non-prohibited bore firearms.

section_title: Suspension and revocation of licences
section_desc: Subject to the provisions of any rules made under this Act, the licensing authority may at any time suspend or revoke a licence granted under Chapter II: if the holder has been convicted of an offence relating to breach of the peace or of an offence under this Act; if the holder is of unsound mind; if the licensing authority deems it necessary for the security of the public peace or for public safety to do so; if the holder has failed to comply with conditions of the licence.

section_title: Power to prohibit carrying of arms in certain cases
section_desc: Whenever it appears to the District Magistrate or any other Magistrate authorised in this behalf that the carrying of arms in any area by any persons or class of persons is likely to disturb the public peace, he may, by general or special order, direct that no person shall carry arms in such area, whether or not such person is the holder of a licence under this Act.

section_title: Punishment for using arms, etc.
section_desc: Whoever uses any arms or ammunition in contravention of section 5 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life or such punishment as provided under any other law, and shall also be liable to fine. Where the offence is committed using prohibited arms, the minimum punishment is ten years.

section_title: Punishment for being member of an unlawful association
section_desc: Whoever is and continues to be a member of an association declared unlawful under this Act, or takes part in meetings of any such association, or contributes to, or receives or solicits any contribution for the purposes of any such association, or in any way assists the operations of any such association, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Punishment for unlawful activities
section_desc: Where an association is declared unlawful by a notification issued under section 3, whoever participates in or commits, advocates, abets, advises or incites the commission of, any unlawful activity shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Punishment for conspiracy, etc.
section_desc: Whoever conspires or attempts to commit, or advocates, abets, advises or incites or knowingly facilitates the commission of, a terrorist act or any act preparatory to a terrorist act, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Punishment for harbouring, etc.
section_desc: Whoever voluntarily harbours or conceals, or attempts to harbour or conceal any person knowing that such person has committed a terrorist act, or in respect of whom a reasonable suspicion exists that he has committed or is likely to commit a terrorist act, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Punishment for being member of terrorist gang or organisation
section_desc: Any person who is a member of a terrorist gang or a terrorist organisation, which is involved in terrorist act, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Enhanced penalties — possession of arms in certain areas
section_desc: Whoever in a notified area, possesses or recruits any person for the purposes of any terrorist act or unlawful activity in any form, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Special Courts
section_desc: The Central Government or a State Government may, for the purpose of providing for speedy trial of offences under this Act, by notification in the Official Gazette, constitute one or more Special Courts for such area or areas, or for such case or class or group of cases, as may be specified in the notification.

section_title: Power to designate organisations as terrorist organisations
section_desc: The Central Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, add an organisation to the Schedule if it believes that it is involved in terrorism. An application for de-listing may be made to the Central Government. The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Tribunal shall review the banning order.

section_title: Offence relating to support given to a terrorist organisation
section_desc: A person commits the offence of support to a terrorist organisation who: invites support for a terrorist organisation; and if the support is not or is not restricted to, the provision of money or other property; or arranges, manages or assists in arranging or managing a meeting which he knows is to be addressed by a person who belongs or professes to belong to a terrorist organisation.

section_title: Power to arrest, search and seize without warrant
section_desc: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, if an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police or any officer of the Central Government or State Government of equivalent rank reasonably suspects that any person has committed an offence under this Act, he may arrest such person without warrant. Such person must be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours.

section_title: Modified application of CrPC — bail
section_desc: In computing the period of ninety days for the purposes of grant of default bail, the time during which the investigation was stayed by any court or injunction granted by a court shall be excluded. No person accused of an offence under Chapters IV and VI of this Act shall be released on bail or bond if the court, after perusing the case diary or the report made under section 173 of CrPC, is of the opinion that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accusation against such person is prima facie true.

act: Prevention of Terrorism Act — key principle
section_title: UAPA Bail — Supreme Court guidelines
section_desc: The Supreme Court in NIA v. Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali (2019) held that for offences under Chapters IV and VI of UAPA, the court must look at the totality of material before it and cannot meticulously appreciate evidence at bail stage. In Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb (2021), the SC held that if the accused has spent an inordinately long time in jail, the constitutional courts can grant bail under Article 21 even in UAPA cases, as the right to speedy trial is a fundamental right.

section_title: Punishment for causing explosion likely to endanger life or property
section_desc: Any person who unlawfully and maliciously causes by any explosive substance an explosion of a nature likely to endanger life or to cause serious injury to property, or conspires to cause any such explosion, shall, whether any injury to person or property has been actually caused or not, be liable to transportation for life or to rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to twenty years, to which fine may be added.

section_title: Punishment for attempt to cause explosion, or for making or keeping explosive with intent to endanger life or property
section_desc: Any person who unlawfully and maliciously: does any act with intent to cause, or conspires to cause, by an explosive substance, an explosion in the United Kingdom or elsewhere of a nature likely to endanger life, or cause serious injury to property; or makes or has in his possession or under his control any explosive substance, with intent by means thereof to endanger life, or cause serious injury to property, in India or elsewhere, or to enable any other person so to do, shall be liable to imprisonment for life or to rigorous imprisonment for a term not exceeding ten years.

section_title: Punishment for making or possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances
section_desc: Any person who makes or knowingly has in his possession or under his control any explosive substance, under such circumstances as to give rise to a reasonable suspicion that he is not making it or does not have it in his possession or under his control for a lawful object, shall, unless he can show that he made it or had it in his possession or under his control for a lawful object, be liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding fourteen years, to which fine may be added.

section_title: Penalties for spying
section_desc: If any person for any purpose prejudicial to the safety or interests of the State: approaches, inspects, passes over or is in the neighbourhood of, or enters any prohibited place; makes any sketch, plan, model, or note which is calculated to be or might be or is intended to be, directly or indirectly, useful to an enemy; obtains, collects, records, publishes or communicates to any other person any secret official code or pass word, or any sketch, plan, model, article, or note, or other document or information which is calculated to be or might be or is intended to be, directly or indirectly, useful to an enemy or which relates to a matter the communication of which is prejudicial to the safety or interests of the State, he shall be guilty of felony.

section_title: Wrongful communication of information
section_desc: If any person having in his possession or control any secret official code or password, or any sketch, plan, model, article, note, document or information which relates to or is used in a prohibited place or relates to anything in such a place, or which has been entrusted in confidence to him by any person holding office under Government, or which he has obtained owing to his position as a person who holds or has held a contract made on behalf of His Majesty or any Government servant, communicates the code, password, sketch, plan, model, article, note, document or information to any person other than a person to whom he is authorised to communicate it, he shall be guilty of a misdemeanour.

section_title: Adjudication
section_desc: The Director or any officer not below the rank of Deputy Director authorised by the Director shall, after conducting an inquiry into the complaint furnished, confirm attachment or make an order of confiscation of property. The Adjudicating Authority shall issue notice to the person whose property is proposed to be confiscated and pass order of confiscation if satisfied that money laundering is proved. Property can include proceeds in any form including foreign exchange.

section_title: Obligations of banking companies, financial institutions and intermediaries
section_desc: Every banking company, financial institution and intermediary shall: maintain a record of all transactions the nature and value of which may be prescribed, whether such transactions comprise a single transaction or a series of transactions integrally connected to each other, and where such series of transactions take place within a month; furnish to the Director such information as may be prescribed; verify and maintain the records of the identity of all its clients.

section_title: Burden of proof
section_desc: In any proceeding relating to proceeds of crime under this Act, the burden of proving that the proceeds of crime are untainted property shall be on the accused. This provision reverses the normal presumption of innocence — the accused must prove that his property is not proceeds of crime. This reverse burden has been upheld by the Supreme Court in Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India (2022).

section_title: Definitions
section_desc: 'Benami property' means property which is the subject matter of a benami transaction and also includes the proceeds from such property; 'benami transaction' means a transaction or an arrangement where a property is transferred to, or is held by, a person, and the consideration for such property has been provided, or paid by, another person; and the property is held for the immediate or future benefit, direct or indirect, of the person who has provided the consideration; 'beneficial owner' means a person for whose benefit the property is held by a benamidar.

section_title: Prohibition of benami transactions
section_desc: No person shall enter into any benami transaction. Nothing in sub-section (1) shall affect the right of any person to enforce a contract entered into before the commencement of the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Amendment Act, 2016, against the person in whose name the property is held. Any property which is subject of a benami transaction shall be liable to be confiscated by the Central Government.

section_title: Punishment for benami transactions
section_desc: Whoever enters into any benami transaction shall: if such transaction is entered into with the intention of defeating the provisions of any law or avoiding payment of statutory dues, be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than one year but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to twenty-five percent of the fair market value of the property.

section_title: Power to make orders
section_desc: The Central Government may by order make provision, either generally or with respect to all foreigners or with respect to any particular foreigner or any prescribed class or description of foreigner, for prohibiting, regulating or restricting the entry of foreigners into India or their departure therefrom or their presence or continued presence therein.

section_title: Penalty
section_desc: If any person contravenes the provisions of this Act or of any order made thereunder, or any direction given in pursuance of this Act or such order, he shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine; and if such person has entered India in contravention of the provisions of this Act, he may be deported from India.

section_title: Refusal of passports, travel documents, etc.
section_desc: The passport authority shall refuse to make an endorsement for visiting any foreign country under sub-section (1) of section 5, or may cancel such endorsement already made, and shall also refuse to issue a passport or travel document and may impound or cause to be impounded or revoke any passport or travel document already issued, in any of the following cases: if the applicant is not a citizen of India; if the passport authority is satisfied that the applicant is in wrongful possession of such passport or travel document; if the applicant has, at any time, been convicted of certain offences.

section_title: Offences and penalties
section_desc: Whoever: knowingly furnishes any false information or suppresses any material information with a view to obtaining a passport or travel document; fails to produce for inspection his passport or travel document when called upon to do so by the prescribed authority; contravenes any condition subject to which a passport or travel document has been issued to him, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.

section_title: Punishment for keeping a brothel or allowing premises to be used as a brothel
section_desc: Any person who keeps or manages, or acts or assists in the keeping or management of, a brothel shall be punishable on first conviction with rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than one year and not more than three years and also with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees. On second conviction: not less than two years and not more than five years and fine.

section_title: Procuring, inducing or taking person for the sake of prostitution
section_desc: Any person who procures or attempts to procure a person, whether by threats or intimidation, or by false pretences, or by fraud, or after administering or causing to be administered to him or her any intoxicant, stupefying or unwholesome drug, matter or thing, or by any other means, with the intent that such person may be or knowing that such person will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse for commercial purposes, shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than three years and not more than seven years and also with fine.

section_title: Punishment for bribery of a public servant by commercial organisations
section_desc: If a commercial organisation gives or promises any undue advantage to a public servant intending to obtain or retain business or an advantage in the conduct of business for such commercial organisation, such commercial organisation shall be punishable with fine. The commercial organisation shall not be guilty if it proves that it had in place adequate procedures designed to prevent persons associated with it from undertaking such conduct.

section_title: Punishment for abetment by public servant of offences defined in section 7 and 11
section_desc: Whoever, being a public servant, abets the commission of an offence punishable under sections 7 and 11 whether or not any offence is committed in consequence of such abetment, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall be not less than three years but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Punishment for abetment of offences defined in section 8
section_desc: Whoever abets any offence punishable under section 8 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall be not less than three years but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Punishment for abetment of offences
section_desc: Whoever abets any offence punishable under this Act, whether or not that offence is committed in consequence of such abetment, shall be punishable with the punishment provided for that offence.

section_title: Habitual offender
section_desc: Whoever having been convicted of an offence punishable under this Act is again convicted of an offence punishable under this Act shall be punished for the second and for every subsequent offence with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than double the minimum punishment prescribed for such offence and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Previous sanction necessary for prosecution
section_desc: No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under sections 7, 11, 13 and 15 alleged to have been committed by a public servant, except with the previous sanction, in the case of a person who is employed in connection with the affairs of the Union, of the Central Government; in the case of a person who is employed in connection with the affairs of a State, of the State Government.

section_title: Disqualification on conviction for certain offences
section_desc: A person convicted of an offence punishable under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, or under the Indian Penal Code in relation to promoting enmity between different groups, or for electoral offences, shall be disqualified, if sentenced to not less than two years of imprisonment, from the date of such conviction and shall continue to be disqualified for a further period of six years since his release.
chapter_title: Disqualifications for Membership of Parliament and State Legislatures

section_title: Grounds for declaring election void
section_desc: Subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), if the High Court is of opinion that any returned candidate has committed any corrupt practice, the election of such returned candidate shall be void. Corrupt practices include bribery, undue influence, use of government machinery, appeal to religion, obtaining assistance from government servants, and booth capturing.

section_title: Corrupt practices
section_desc: The following shall be deemed to be corrupt practices for the purposes of this Act: (1) Bribery — giving gratification to vote in a particular manner; (2) Undue influence — direct or indirect interference with free exercise of any electoral right; (3) Appeal on grounds of religion, race, caste, community or language; (4) Promotion of enmity between classes in connection with election; (5) Publication of false statement concerning conduct or character of a candidate; (6) Hiring or procuring of vehicles; (7) Booth capturing.

section_title: Cyber terrorism — detailed elements
section_desc: For Section 66F ITA: The offence of cyber terrorism requires: (1) access to a computer resource without authorisation; (2) the intent must be to threaten the unity, integrity, sovereignty or security of India; OR intent to strike terror in people; OR to create widespread panic. Methods include using malware to disrupt critical infrastructure — power grids, financial systems, communication networks, water supply. Life imprisonment is mandatory if death results from cyber terrorism.

section_title: Protected system
section_desc: The appropriate Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare any computer resource which directly or indirectly affects the facility of Critical Information Infrastructure, to be a protected system. Any person who secures access or attempts to secure access to a protected system in contravention of the provisions of this section shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine.

section_title: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team
section_desc: The Central Government shall, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint an agency of the Government to be called the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team. CERT-In shall serve as the national agency for performing the following functions in the area of cyber security: collection, analysis and dissemination of information on cyber incidents; forecast and alerts of cyber security incidents; emergency measures for handling cyber security incidents; coordination of cyber incidents response activities.

act: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
section_title: Due diligence to be observed by intermediaries
section_desc: An intermediary shall observe the following due diligence while discharging its duties: publish on its website, mobile application, or both, privacy policy and user agreement for access or usage of the computer resource; inform its users about the periodic takedown of unlawful content; not deploy or install or modify hardware or software to gain access without consent; report cyber security incidents. Significant Social Media Intermediaries (SSMIs) must appoint Grievance Officer, Nodal Officer and Chief Compliance Officer.

act: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
section_title: Additional due diligence by significant social media intermediary
section_desc: A significant social media intermediary shall: appoint a Chief Compliance Officer (Indian resident) responsible for ensuring compliance with the Act and Rules; appoint a Nodal Contact Person for coordination with law enforcement agencies; appoint a Resident Grievance Officer for receiving and handling complaints from users in India; publish a monthly compliance report mentioning content removed or access disabled; enable identification of the first originator of an information on its platform when required by court or competent authority.

act: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
section_title: Procedure in relation to Juvenile Justice Board
section_desc: If a child alleged to be in conflict with law is produced before a Magistrate or Court other than the Board, such Magistrate or Court shall without any delay ensure that the child is sent to the Board within twenty-four hours. Any officer of a special juvenile police unit or of the designated child welfare police officer shall produce a child alleged to be in conflict with law before the Board without unnecessary delay and within twenty-four hours of such arrest.

act: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
section_title: Bail for child alleged to be in conflict with law
section_desc: When any person accused of a bailable or non-bailable offence, and apparently a child, is arrested or detained or appears or is brought before a Board, such person shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, or in any other law for the time being in force, be released on bail with or without surety or placed under the supervision of a probation officer or under the care of any fit person. However, release on bail shall be denied if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that the release is likely to bring that person into association with any known criminal or expose the child to moral, physical or psychological danger.

act: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
section_title: Orders that may be passed regarding child in conflict with law
section_desc: Where a Board is satisfied on inquiry that a child irrespective of age has committed a petty offence, or a serious offence, or a child below the age of sixteen years has committed a heinous offence, it may pass orders: allow the child to go home after advice and admonition; direct the child to participate in group counselling and similar activities; order the child to perform community service; order the child or the parent or the guardian to pay fine; direct the child to be released on probation of good conduct under the supervision of any parent, guardian or fit person; direct the child to be sent to a special home.

act: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
section_title: Restoration of child
section_desc: The restoration and protection of a child shall be the prime objective of any order made by a Child Welfare Committee or the Board. A child in conflict with law may be restored to parents or guardian or fit persons or foster family if the Board so directs. Child Welfare Committee shall restore a child in need of care and protection to his family if it is in the best interest of the child.
